target.title: fix(wizard): reject loose gateway port input
target.body:
Closes #98681

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running manual setup could enter a gateway port such as `1e3` or `0x1000` and have the wizard accept it but persist a different port.

## Why This Change Was Made

The setup wizard now uses the same strict base-10 integer parser for gateway port validation and persistence. This keeps valid decimal TCP ports unchanged while rejecting loose numeric syntax before it can be truncated by `parseInt`.

## User Impact

Manual setup users now get the existing port-range validation message for loose numeric port input instead of silently saving an unintended gateway port.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: manual gateway setup rejects loose numeric port input instead of saving a truncated value.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/wizard/setup.gateway-config.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local`
- Observed result:
  - Focused Vitest passed: `src/wizard/setup.gateway-config.test.ts` 13 tests passed, including `rejects loose gateway port input: 1e3` and `rejects loose gateway port input: 0x1000`.
  - `git diff --check` passed with no output.
  - Autoreview reported `autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported` and `overall: patch is correct (0.86)`.
- Not tested / proof gaps:
  - Did not run full repository checks or broad typecheck, per scoped small-change validation.
  - Local `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` timed out after 124s while hydrating this isolated worktree, but it left enough dependencies for the focused Vitest command above to run and pass. No lockfile changes were made.
